transcript:
This message comes from Thumbtack.
Avoiding your unfinished home projects
because you're not sure where to start?
Thumbtack knows homes so you don't have to.
Don't know the difference
between matte paint finish and satin,
or what that clunking sound from your dryer is?
With Thumbtack, you don't have to be a home pro,
you just have to hire one.
You can hire top-rated pros,
see price estimates, and read reviews, all on the app.
Download today.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines, every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Polls are opening on the West Coast this hour,
including in California and Oregon.
Washington State and Alaska will open next hour.
Hawaii's polls will open in two hours.
Democrats are vying with Republicans
for control of Congress, and PR Stephen Fowler reports
this year's midterm elections are consequential.
It broke the record
for the most expensive election in history,
where the president's approval ratings
are at near-record lows,
and a record number of lawmakers
have chosen to retire this year,
and that's before voters may retire some more.
At the start of the midterm cycle,
the fight for control of Congress
was centered around the usual tight races and places
in states like Georgia, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania.
But now, as the final votes are cast,
the competitive landscape stretches deep
into more conservative places like Kansas, Texas, and Iowa.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Des Moines.
The state of Florida is moving some polling sites today
because of severe weather.
Heavy rain is still falling in several counties
on Florida's Atlantic coast, triggering flooding.
36 states are holding gubernatorial contests today.
19 incumbent governors are also leaving office,
and PR's Larry Kaplow reports the gubernatorial winners
could play a role in President Trump's future agenda.
Currently, 26 states are led by Republican governors,
and many have used their power to do things
like increase local law enforcement cooperation with ICE
or to provide voter data to the Trump administration.
Some of the country's 24 Democratic governors
have limited cooperation with ICE
or joined lawsuits that have helped block Trump tariffs
or administration cuts in money for healthcare.
Some of the closest gubernatorial races
are in Wisconsin and Kansas,
where Democrats are term-limited,
and Republicans have a chance to flip the office.
Democrats are eyeing opportunities
to pick up governors' offices in states,
including Nevada, Iowa, Georgia, and Ohio.
Larry Kaplow, NPR News.
Stocks open mix this morning as Apple shares take a hit.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average
fell more than 330 points in early trading.
Apple shares open lower despite the company's
better-than-expected profits in its most recent quarter.
In an earnings call late Monday,
Apple said it was enjoying strong demand for iPhones,
but the company warned of supply constraints
in the current quarter caused by global demand
for memory chips.
Saudi Aramco earned a gusher of profits during the summer,
thanks to high prices for crude oil and refined products.
The U.S. war with Iran has triggered a spike
in energy prices, but Saudi Aramco has managed
to maintain exports, in part, by using a pipeline
to bypass the snarled Strait of Hormuz.
Asian stocks were mixed overnight, up in Hong Kong,
but down in Shanghai and Seoul.
Tokyo stock market was closed for a holiday.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
This is NPR.
President Trump says the U.S. will stop providing Israel
with military aid after the end of this year.
He spoke this morning on Fox News.
Trump says he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
have reached the agreement.
President Trump's special envoy, Steve Whitcoff,
says the U.S. will mediate talks between Ukraine
and Russia next week.
Writing online, he says the working-level talks
will be held in Abu Dhabi, and they'll focus
on post-war security arrangements.
He says these include de-escalation, humanitarian efforts,
and next steps toward peace.
New York State has reported its first measles-associated
death in more than 30 years,
and Piers Maria Godoy has more.
Public health officials in New York State
announced the death on Monday evening.
They did not release details of the child's age
or vaccination status.
Four weeks ago, New York Governor Kathy Hochul
declared a state of emergency in response
to the measles outbreak across parts of New York
and in neighboring states.
As of October 24th, the state had confirmed
178 measles cases this year,
including eight in New York City.
Next door, Pennsylvania has reported five measles-associated
deaths this year.
Measles is one of the most contagious diseases known.
Across the U.S., nearly 5,000 measles cases
have been reported so far this year,
though infectious disease experts believe
the true number is much higher,
with many more cases likely going unreported.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
- And I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.
- We will learn something on election night,
but not everything.
There's a lot we will not know,
especially when it comes to close races,
and we'll know much more the next morning
and the morning after that.
So save yourself a little time scrolling
and listen to Up First.
We'll be there when you wake up each and every morning
this week with the latest midterm election news.
